references.text: The Levites are brought forward to Aaron to serve him, establishing their role as assistants to the priests at the sanctuary.
The Levites are given responsibility for the tabernacle and its service, and they shall camp around the dwelling of the testimony.
The Levites are given to Aaron and his sons to perform service in the tent of meeting.
The name 'Levi' is explained from the Hebrew 'livyah' (attachment), playing on the wordplay 'veyillavu' (they shall attach themselves to you) in the text.
The tabernacle is called 'the dwelling of the testimony,' the same expression as 'ohel ha'edut' in this verse.
The tent of the testimony is mentioned as the place where the Lord meets Moses, the same place where Aaron and his sons shall serve.
Aaron and his sons are chosen for the priestly service, which the Levites are to support in their ministry.
